critical_code_review_comments: routes/google_oauth.py _build_redirect_uri() forces 'https://' from the request Host header. Excellent for K8s/Cloudflare TLS-termination, but a request arriving over plain HTTP (e.g. internal health check via Host: stageetudiant.com on port 80) would still get https://… in the redirect_uri — fine in practice, but worth a one-line code comment saying 'we deliberately ignore request.url.scheme because the public ingress is always TLS'.

routes/google_oauth.py db.oauth_states: TTL index on created_at is NOT created in this module — server.py only adds an index on users.google_id (line 1281). The system prompt mentions 'TTL 10 min' but I don't see `db.oauth_states.create_index([('created_at',1)], expireAfterSeconds=600)` anywhere. RECOMMENDATION: add the TTL index in startup (init_indexes) to avoid orphan rows from interrupted login flows. Currently states are deleted only on successful consumption.

routes/google_oauth.py stores `created_at` as ISO string — Mongo TTL requires a real BSON Date type. If the TTL index gets added later, change to `datetime.now(timezone.utc)` (no .isoformat()) for proper expiration semantics.

ChooseRolePage.jsx lines 16-22 call navigate() synchronously during render — this triggers React warning 'Cannot update during render'. Move into useEffect(() => { if (user?.role) navigate(...) }, [user]).

AuthContext.jsx lines 27-43: when the URL has #token=…, after storing token the code does NOT re-trigger checkAuth() — it falls into checkAuth() naturally because the token is now in localStorage, but the early-return for session_id branch happens before checkAuth runs. Verified working in browser test, but a useState rerender of `loading` after token write would make state more deterministic.

server.py /auth/choose-role accepts only 'candidate'/'company' — admins created via Google OAuth (with role=null) can't elevate themselves here (good). But there is no path to mark a Google-created user as admin; currently only ensure_owner_admin auto-seeds the owner. Likely intentional, but consider a guarded path or a CLI script for production safety.

rca of the issue: N/A — no bugs found. This iteration is a clean refactor (server.py 3543→2967 lines via 6 new route modules) plus a brand-new custom Google OAuth route. Placeholder GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID makes both /auth/google and /auth/google/callback return 503 (correctly guarded by _is_configured()); when real creds are provided, the route is designed to build redirect_uri from request Host (no hardcoded URL — verified by code reading at lines 34-38). State is stored in db.oauth_states with one-time consumption (find_one_and_delete). JWT is returned to frontend via URL fragment #token=… (cleaner than query string — not logged by proxies). All 12 split-regression endpoints continue to work identically after the move.
